As patients develop acute lung injury and progress into ARDS, their lungs become progressively recruited and develop shunts, which leads to decreased functional lung volume. They are using pressure-cycled ventilation over volume-cycled to maintain consistent flow to all patients on the other end of the ventilator, along with high PEEP (Positive End-Expiratory Pressure) and low driving pressure (to achieve lung protection). The current thinking is that COVID patients are PEEP responders and that COVID patients are requiring increased levels of PEEP beyond what is normally given to patients with ARDS. This is one aspect of COVID that sets it apart from Influenza related pneumonia.

This treatment is pretty consistent across the board from what ER and ICU physicians are reporting. So, this part of his story lines up with the treatment they are currently using. His contention is the rational behind using the increased PEEP on COVID patients. Why are these patients appearing to have O2 starvation and not typical respiratory failure that requires assisted breathing?

It is worth noting that the reason I believe this physician is concerned is because usually once a COVID patient ia placed on a ventilator, the outcome is poor despite their efforts. This is being reported by multiple physicians caring for these patients in acute respiratory distress. Not many of these patients recover once they reach this point in the disease process. I can understand the frustration and wanting to consider whether they can improve outcomes by taking step back and reviewing their protocol. Above all, do not harm. Unfortunately, he is probably so busy he doesn't have time to consider other options for treatment.

I think this physician needs to be heard by his community. Why he felt the need to go public using the platform he chose, I question. He just puts his own job in jeopardy and it lessens his credibility among colleagues - IMHO so don't attack me. However, he does bring up observations that need to be explored. At this point, it is a tough call because patients on ventilators have nothing to lose by taking another look at the treatment modality being used. But, on the other hand, there is no time to experiment on critically ill patients without getting your ass sued by deviating from standard treatment protocol. And, you don't get a do-over if you make the wrong choice. COVID patients often quickly degrade so it is difficult to take a step back and rethink this.

It is easy for us not on the front lines of this fight to armchair quarterback physicians who are in the midst of medical emergencies where they only have a couple of plays in the playbook and no time to consider new ones. Don't forget, they have lives at stake and do not have the luxury to experiment. Lawyers, politicians, big pharma, and the public has seen to that.
